source.title: Bayesian predictive densities for linear regression models under α-divergence loss: some results and open problems

accepted.question_text: In the normal linear regression prediction setting considered in the paper, assume the design matrices satisfy assumption (AS1): m ≥ k ≥ 3, n = mN for some positive integer N, and X = 1_N ⊗ X̃ so that the observed and future design matrices have the repeated-design structure used by Komaki (2001). Under α-divergence loss D_α with −1 < α < 1, does the predictive density based on the shrinkage prior π_S,1(β, σ²) = (β′X̃′X̃β)^{1−k/2}(σ²)^{−2} improve on the best invariant predictive density, namely the generalized Bayes predictive density based on the right invariant prior π_I,1(β, σ²) = (σ²)^{−1}?
accepted.context_brief: Shrinkage versus invariant prediction under α-divergence

evidence.quote: Problem 1 Under the assumption (AS1) and the Dα loss for −1 < α < 1, does the predictive density with respect to the same shrinkage prior given by (1.8) improve on the best invariant predictive density with respect to (1.9)?

accepted.question_text: Under D_1 loss in the same predictive-density estimation problem for normal linear regression with unknown variance, and in the low-dimensional cases k = 1 or k = 2, the paper notes that the best invariant predictive density is still inadmissible because a better non-Bayesian predictive density can be constructed. The open question is whether one can construct improved Bayesian predictive densities that dominate the best invariant predictive density in these cases k = 1 and k = 2.
accepted.context_brief: Bayesian improvement for k equals 1 or 2 under D1

evidence.quote: Problem 2-1 Under D1 loss, even if k = 1, 2, the best invariant predictive density remains inadmissible because an improved non-Bayesian predictive density is easily found. (See Section 4.) Can we find improved Bayesian predictive densities for this case (k = 1, 2)?
For Problem 2-1, we will give an exact solution.

accepted.question_text: When the parameter dimension is k = 1 or k = 2 and the loss is α-divergence D_α with −1 ≤ α < 1, does the best invariant predictive density remain inadmissible? If it does, which Bayesian predictive density or class of Bayesian predictive densities improves upon it?

evidence.quote: Problem 2-2 Under k = 1, 2 and the Dα loss with −1 ≤ α < 1, does the best invariant predictive density keep inadmissibility? If so, which Bayesian predictive density improve it?
We could not solve Problem 2-2 in this paper

accepted.question_text: For predictive density estimation under α-divergence loss D_α with |α| < 1 in the canonical normal model, is there an identity or structural relationship analogous to the one George, Liang, and Xu (2006) used for Kullback-Leibler loss, namely a relationship linking predictive-risk reduction to the risk-reduction theory for estimating a multivariate normal mean vector?
accepted.context_brief: Analogue of KL risk-reduction identity for general α

evidence.quote: George, Liang and Xu (2006) used some techniques including the heat equation and Stein’s identity, and eventually found a new identity which links KL risk reduction to Stein’s unbiased estimate of risk reduction.

Hence we expect that there should exist an analogous relationship between the prediction problem under the Dα loss for |α| < 1 and the problem of estimating the mean vector. As far as we know, this is still an open problem.
